# Perplexity + GrowthBook
Date: 2026-10-16 | Duration: 63.52000045776367m

## Summary
Perplexity evaluated GrowthBook against an agent-first experimentation workflow covering experiment creation, registration, launch, analysis, debugging, power calculations, result retrieval, and export without using the UI. GrowthBook said its API supports most lifecycle actions, with published agent tooling, a CLI, and MCP access, while power-analysis APIs and broader guardrails remain incomplete. Governance features include project roles, scoped tokens, OAuth, audit logs, drafts, and environment-specific approvals. Snowflake and ClickHouse are supported, and Git-managed definitions, DBT synchronization, and external analysis workflows are available. Gaps include native writeback of computed results, metric-group synchronization, smoother Git-based experiment plans, and tooling for a GitHub experiment-history repository. Perplexity also discussed EPO migration uncertainty, vendor responsiveness, and AI guidance for metric selection and analysis timing. Alexis Weill and Noah Yonack requested roadmap timelines; Jeremy Dorn offered follow-up, while Christian Liebenow will send the recording and summary.

## Keywords
Agent-led experimentation, GrowthBook, MCP server, Code-managed metrics, Warehouse-native analytics, Experimentation APIs
